descriptor: Premium branded apple grower & plant-variety IP licensor (ENVY, JAZZ, JOLI) · FY ends 31 Dec · reported in NZD · exiting NZ/Fiji/Pacific fresh produce (pending Commerce Commission clearance)

kpis.label: H1 FY2026 Net Loss
kpis.note: -29.6m disposal loss on T&G Fresh sale; continuing ops was -0.9m

kpis.label: NTA per share
kpis.note: 0.68x NTA -- asset backing is the DCF's second leg

kpis.label: Owner FCF (continuing, FY2025)

kpis.note: 50/50 blend of owner-FCF and asset (book x P/B) legs

sections.title: Scale vs. Profitability
sections.subtitle: T&G is a NZ$1.3-1.6bn revenue business earning low single-digit net margins -- absolute profit is charted separately so it isn't swamped by the revenue line

charts.title: Revenue & YoY Growth
charts.annotation: H1 FY2026 revenue (572.3m) is CONTINUING-OPERATIONS ONLY after the 31-Jul-2026 agreement to sell T&G Fresh's NZ, Fiji and Pacific businesses; every FY bar and H1 FY2025 are whole-company. Like-for-like continuing growth was +2.6%, not the ~38% drop the raw H1 bars imply.

charts.title: Gross / Operating / Net Margin
charts.annotation: FY2023 (-3.4% operating margin) is Cyclone Gabrielle: the storm destroyed ~13% of Hawke's Bay planted hectares and drove a NZ$45.6m operating loss.

charts.title: Net Income & EBITDA (absolute NZ$)
charts.annotation: Net income includes NZ$5-6m/yr of non-controlling interests (mainly the Worldwide Fruit UK 50% JV) that never reaches T&G parent shareholders. FY2023 Cyclone Gabrielle and H1 FY2026's -30.5m disposal-loss print are both real but non-recurring shocks, not trend.

sections.title: Strategic Pivot: Apples & VentureFruit
sections.subtitle: management's own framing -- branded fruit and plant-variety IP licensing over low-margin produce trading

charts.title: EBITDA Margin
charts.annotation: H1 FY2026 EBITDA margin of ~6.1% is on continuing operations; management's base-case DCF path assumes this climbs to 9% by FY2031 as VentureFruit reaches breakeven and stranded corporate costs are cut.

charts.title: Operating Cash Flow vs Reported FCF vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF (DCF JSON) deducts full IFRS-16 lease principal from reported FCF and was negative in 6 of the last 7 years -- replanting capex and lease payments consistently exceed operating cash flow. FY2025's reported FCF of 59.3m is a capex-suppressed peak (32.6m vs 48-107m in FY2021-24), which is why the DCF's base_fcf uses the continuing-ops 2.5m figure, not this series.

charts.title: CapEx (Orchard & Facility Investment)
charts.annotation: Capex swings 33-107m/yr with orchard replanting cycles (ENVY plantings) and post-harvest facility investment (Whakatu, Hawke's Bay, Nelson); FY2025's 32.6m is below the historical range and is expected to normalise toward ~3% of revenue.

sections.title: Balance Sheet & Asset Backing
sections.subtitle: the DCF's asset leg rests on book value and NTA, not the going-concern earnings alone

charts.title: NTA per Share (vs NZ$2.40 current price)
charts.annotation: Share price NZ$2.40 (4-Sep-2026) is not plotted as a series (no time series exists for it in this dataset) but sits at ~0.68x the latest NTA/share shown here. T&G has closed above 1.0x book only once in ten fiscal year-ends (FY2016). The DCF's asset leg (parent book x exit P/B) is calibrated to this history, not to a re-rating.

charts.title: Total Debt vs Cash
charts.annotation: TotalDebt excludes NZ$165-210m of IFRS-16 lease liabilities (treated as an operating cost in the DCF, not debt). Dec-2025 net debt of ~146m is expected to fall to ~70m once T&G Fresh sale proceeds (~76m) are received and applied to debt, including a NZ$20.8m related-party BayWa loan.

charts.title: Shareholders' Equity
charts.annotation: Equity fell from FY2021's 573.6m peak as Cyclone Gabrielle losses (FY2023) and ongoing thin/negative earnings eroded retained earnings; the 5-year equity CAGR is -0.6%, materially below the +2.0% revenue CAGR over the same period.

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Total sales of produce, commissions, services, royalties and plant-variety licences.

For T&G Global: every FY bar (and the H1 FY2025 bar) is WHOLE-COMPANY, including the NZ/Fiji/Pacific fresh produce businesses agreed for sale on 31 July 2026 (pending Commerce Commission clearance). H1 FY2026's 572.3m is CONTINUING OPERATIONS ONLY -- the like-for-like comparison is +2.6% growth, not a ~38% collapse.

What to watch:

  • Apples segment revenue growth (67% of FY2025 group revenue, growing)
  • VentureFruit royalty/licence revenue -- small (~1-2%) but the strategic focus
  • FY2026 full-year revenue will step down structurally once the T&G Fresh sale completes -- management has explicitly flagged this as NOT a like-for-like decline

margins.title: Gross / Operating / Net Margin
margins.content:
Profitability at three levels of the income statement, as a percent of revenue.

For T&G Global: this is a structurally thin-margin business -- net margin has ranged from -3.5% to +1.6% over FY2019-2025, never exceeding ~1.6%. The strategic pivot to branded Apples and VentureFruit IP licensing exists specifically to lift these margins.

What to watch:

  • FY2023's -3.4% operating margin is Cyclone Gabrielle, a one-off weather disaster, not a trend break
  • Margin expansion as VentureFruit's royalty model (high incremental margin) scales
  • Whether corporate/'Other' segment losses (-45m FY2025) shrink post-divestment

profit.title: Net Income & EBITDA (Absolute)
profit.content:
Absolute NZ$ profit figures, shown separately from the revenue chart because at ~1% net margins the profit line is invisible next to a NZ$1.3-1.6bn revenue bar.

For T&G Global: Net income is TOTAL including non-controlling interests (NCI) -- NZ$5-6m/yr, mainly the 50%-owned Worldwide Fruit UK JV -- which never reaches T&G's own shareholders. H1 FY2026's -30.5m headline loss is dominated by a -29.6m non-cash disposal/impairment loss on reclassifying T&G Fresh as held-for-sale; continuing operations alone lost only -0.9m.

What to watch:

  • FY2023 (-46.6m, Cyclone Gabrielle) and H1 FY2026 (-30.5m, disposal loss) are both one-off shocks
  • EBITDA is far less volatile than net income -- most of the swing is D&A, interest and one-off impairments below the EBITDA line

ebitdaMargin.title: EBITDA Margin
ebitdaMargin.content:
EBITDA as a percent of revenue, post-IFRS-16 (lease costs are charged as an operating expense in the DCF, so this margin is NOT pre-rent).

For T&G Global: the DCF's base case assumes continuing-ops EBITDA margin rises from ~7.0% in FY2026 to 9.0% by FY2031 as VentureFruit reaches breakeven and corporate overhead is cut following the T&G Fresh divestment.

What to watch:

  • Whether the FY2025 group margin of 7.1% (110.1m/1,558.7m) can be sustained on a smaller, continuing-ops-only revenue base
  • VentureFruit segment margin -- currently negative (-2.4m FY2025 operating loss on 9.0m revenue)

fcf.title: Operating Cash Flow vs Reported FCF vs Owner FCF
fcf.content:
Three different cash-generation measures: raw operating cash flow, reported free cash flow (OCF less capex), and the DCF's owner FCF (which additionally deducts full IFRS-16 lease principal payments -- T&G's leases are a real, recurring cash cost of doing business, not a financing curiosity).

For T&G Global: Owner FCF was negative in 6 of the last 7 fiscal years. FY2025's headline reported FCF of 59.3m looks strong but sits on a capex-suppressed year (32.6m vs a 48-107m range in FY2021-24) plus a working-capital release -- the DCF instead bases its FY2026 starting point on the continuing-operations owner FCF of just 2.5m.

What to watch:

  • Capex normalising back toward 3% of revenue (~35-45m) as replanting resumes
  • Whether owner FCF turns durably positive as VentureFruit's asset-light royalty model scales

capex.title: Capital Expenditure
capex.content:
Cash spent on orchard replanting, post-harvest facilities and other property, plant and equipment.

For T&G Global: capex is lumpy with the orchard replanting cycle -- FY2022's 106.7m includes a heavy ENVY planting push, while FY2025's 32.6m is unusually low and is not expected to persist.

What to watch:

  • Capex intensity as a share of revenue reverting toward the DCF's assumed 3.0-3.3% (base/bear cases)
  • Investment tied to JOLI apple launch and NZ crop volume growth (+24% in 2026 from maturing plantings)

priceToNta.title: NTA per Share vs Share Price
priceToNta.content:
Net tangible assets (NTA) per share compared to the traded share price -- the key gauge of whether the market is pricing T&G above, at, or below its tangible book value.

For T&G Global: this comparison is central to the DCF, which blends a going-concern earnings leg 50/50 with an asset leg (parent book value x a history-disciplined exit price-to-book multiple). Reported NTA of NZ$3.53/share (FY2025, includes NCI) vs a NZ$2.40 price implies ~0.68x; on the parent-only book basis used inside the DCF (NZ$3.66/share at Jun-2026) the ratio is similar. The stock has closed above 1.0x book only once in ten fiscal year-ends (FY2016).

What to watch:

  • Land and buildings are carried at independent valuation (~232m) -- a real asset floor behind the orchard estate
  • BayWa AG (~74% holder) is a forced seller under financial distress; the NZ Takeovers Code requires any acquirer of that stake to offer all minority holders the same price, which is the practical route by which the asset leg could be realised
  • The exit P/B used in the DCF (bear 0.45x / base 0.70x / bull 0.95x) is capped at what T&G has actually traded at over the last decade, not an aspirational re-rating

debt.title: Total Debt vs Cash
debt.content:
Interest-bearing borrowings compared to cash and equivalents on hand.

For T&G Global: TotalDebt excludes IFRS-16 lease liabilities (NZ$165-210m), which the DCF instead treats as an operating cost inside cash flows. Net debt is highly seasonal -- ~146m at the Dec-2025 audited trough vs ~235m at the Jun-2026 unaudited seasonal peak (inventory build, grower advances) -- and the DCF anchors to the Dec-2025 trough since it matches the FY2026 flow build.

What to watch:

  • Expected ~76m of T&G Fresh disposal proceeds earmarked for debt paydown, including a NZ$20.8m related-party BayWa loan
  • Bank facilities are secured through to 2028, reducing near-term refinancing risk despite the ownership overhang

equity.title: Shareholders' Equity
equity.content:
Total book equity attributable to all shareholders, including non-controlling interests.

For T&G Global: equity fell from a FY2021 peak of 573.6m as Cyclone Gabrielle losses and years of thin or negative earnings eroded retained earnings faster than revenue grew (5yr equity CAGR -0.6% vs 5yr revenue CAGR +2.0%) -- the growth-divergence the DCF JSON specifically flags.

What to watch:

  • Whether equity stabilises now that Cyclone Gabrielle is fully absorbed and margins are recovering (FY2025 net income back to +16.0m)
  • Impact of the ~34.4m H1 FY2026 disposal-group impairment, taken through the income statement ahead of the T&G Fresh sale completing

dcf.base_sublabel: Owner FCF — continuing operations, after lease cash
dcf.model_approach_note: This valuation is a 50/50 BLEND of two legs: (1) an owner-FCF DCF on the continuing Apples/VentureFruit business, and (2) an asset leg (parent book value per share × a 10-year-history-disciplined exit price-to-book). The blend was applied because the pure earnings DCF alone tripped the model's own sanity check — it implied 0.26x book, below the 10-year trading minimum of 0.42x, effectively valuing NZ$232m of independently-valued land and buildings, and the ENVY/JAZZ orchard estate, at less than any buyer has ever paid. The sliders below move only the going-concern leg; the DCF JSON's non_operating_assets field carries the asset-leg blend term at full (100%) weight even though the model applies it at 50%, so moving a slider shows roughly 2x the true sensitivity of the blended intrinsic value (see inputs.notes, "SLIDER NOTE", in the DCF JSON).
